record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: After very high energy collisions, can domains of disordered chiral condensate form in an effective pion-and-sigma field theory, and would such domains produce observable bunches of particles with a definite charge, such as neutral-particle bunches?

evidence.quote: Another approach is to consider an effective field theory of hadrons, for instance in the framework of a σ-model of pions and sigma resonances.

This leads to dramatic predictions, like the formation of domains of disordered chiral condensates(DCC) following a very high energy collision. In more practical terms, one could observe bunches of particles with definite charge, e.g. neutrals. This picture may remain a theoretician dream, but it is worth investigating its consequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an effective field theory of low-energy hadrons formulated as a linear sigma model whose dynamical fields are the pion isotriplet π=(π¹,π²,π³) and a scalar σ field, with a chirally symmetric potential whose vacuum spontaneously breaks SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R down to the diagonal isospin SU(2) and selects a preferred direction in the (σ,π) order-parameter space. Suppose that following a very high-energy hadronic or nuclear collision the system is initially driven into a hot, approximately chirally symmetric configuration and then rapidly cooled (quenched), so that long-wavelength modes of the chiral order parameter (σ,π) may temporarily relax along directions misaligned with the true vacuum direction, forming spatial regions ("domains") of disoriented chiral condensate (DCC).

(a) Within this effective field theory, determine whether such DCC domains can form as a dynamical consequence of the quench, and characterize their typical size, lifetime, and number distribution.

(b) Determine whether the decay of these domains produces observable bunches of pions with anomalous isospin composition — in particular, events containing a definite charge fraction such as bunches of nearly all neutral pions — and predict the resulting event-by-event distribution of the neutral-pion fraction f = N(π⁰)/N(π), to be contrasted with the binomial baseline f-distribution expected from isospin-symmetric independent emission.
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical mechanisms for DCC formation in a quenched linear sigma model are well developed and predict anomalous neutral-pion fraction distributions. However, dedicated experimental searches (MiniMax at the Tevatron, WA98 at CERN SPS, and subsequent RHIC/LHC analyses) have not produced a confirmed DCC signal, and reviews as recent as Mohanty–Serreau (2005) and later describe DCC observation as still eluding experiment. The question of whether DCC domains genuinely form and yield observable neutral bunches therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Disoriented Chiral Condensate: Theory and Experiment
status_evidence.snippet: Although the generation of disoriented chiral condensates ... is quite natural in the theory of strong interactions, they have so far eluded experiments in accelerators and cosmic rays.
status_evidence.claim: DCC formation predicted theoretically but not yet observed experimentally.

status_evidence.title: Search for Disoriented Chiral Condensates in 158 AGeV Pb+Pb collisions (WA98)
status_evidence.snippet: In a sample of 212646 events, no clear DCC signal could be distinguished.
status_evidence.claim: WA98 found no clear DCC signal in Pb+Pb collisions.
